obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise (company merchant accounts)
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25) Section A.3.1; acquirer agreement (contract term, fictional)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to card data or a payment system at owned or leased hotels, or in the CRS card vault
deadline: Immediately (WTDIC A.3.1); acquirer agreement: within 24 hours of suspicion (fictional)
notify: Acquiring bank risk line, then in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - card brand rule applied through the acquirer agreement; the timing term is contractual
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system; applies to merchants and service providers
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (North America contact in Table 1.1), normally through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - as merchant and as service provider
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0, Section A.2.1 and Attachment A
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the acquirer, with containment and remediation steps and dates
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days
notify: Visa, through the acquirer's upload tools
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0, Sections A.5.1 and A.5.3
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the acquirer (PFI reports go directly to Visa). The PFI must not be affiliated with the company or have provided QSA, advisory, or security services to it in the past 3 years
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required; rules out the current and 2025 QSA firms
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance; General Counsel

obligation: Independent investigation (if Visa requires one instead of a PFI)
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring an independent investigation
deadline: Contract a qualified investigator within 5 business days
notify: Visa (reports go directly to Visa)
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Other card brands (Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per each brand's rules; timing not verified here. Follow the acquirer's instructions and treat 24 hours as the working target
notify: Brand, normally through the acquirer
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

trigger: The incident involves a vulnerability in the payment processing system (legacy POS, PMS payment interface, terminals)
deadline: Immediately (recommended)
notify: Legacy POS vendor; cloud POS vendor; PMS vendor; P2PE solution provider; payment gateway

obligation: Evidence preservation requests to hosting and cloud providers
trigger: Compromise involves systems hosted by third parties
deadline: As soon as possible (logs roll over)
notify: Cloud providers A and B; PMS vendor; legacy POS vendor

trigger: Suspected compromise of systems the company operates for an owner, or of an owner's merchant account
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (fictional term); the company prepares the owner's acquirer notice
notify: Owner of each affected managed hotel

obligation: Franchisee notice of a compromise of brand systems
citation: Franchise agreements signed since 2022 (contract term, fictional); side letters for 212 older agreements (POAM-012)
trigger: Suspected compromise of the PMS tenant, CRS, card vault, or managed network affecting a franchised hotel's guests or card data
deadline: Within 72 hours of suspicion (fictional term); facts needed for the franchisee's own notices as they become available
notify: Each affected franchisee (owner and designated hotel administrator)

trigger: Suspected compromise of the CRS or booking engine services affecting a client's guests or card data
deadline: Within 72 hours of suspicion (fictional term)
notify: Each affected independent hotel client

obligation: Franchisee incident report to the brand (inbound)
citation: Brand technology standard BS-TECH-06 under the franchise agreement (fictional term)
trigger: A franchisee suspects a compromise that may affect brand systems or guest data
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (fictional term)
notify: Company franchise incident line

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected guests and staff reside
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination of a breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above state-set counts or of any size, depending on the state
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or regulator where the state requires it

trigger: Notices above state-set counts
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies

obligation: State third-party agent and service provider duties
trigger: A breach of a system the company maintains for franchisees or SL-2 clients (outbound), or of a vendor system holding company data (inbound)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Outbound: franchisees and clients whose data it is. Inbound: the vendor notifies the company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides when the company acts as an agent
owner: General Counsel; Director of Third-Party Risk Management

trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information of Florida residents: name with an identity document number, or name with a card number in combination with any required security code (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (unless delayed under (4)(b) or waived under (4)(c)); 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email, with the date range, the information involved, and a contact
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with a synopsis, the Florida count, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if this path is used; unlikely for card and ID data. Counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

trigger: Direct notice would cost more than $250,000, more than 500,000 people are affected, or there is no mailing or email address
deadline: With the individual notice deadline
notify: Conspicuous notice on the company website plus print and broadcast media where affected individuals reside

trigger: A breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent: inbound from vendors; outbound where the company maintains personal information for franchisees or SL-2 clients
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the agent may give the covered entity's notices on its behalf
notify: Inbound: the company. Outbound: each franchisee or client that is the covered entity
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides the company's role per data set
owner: General Counsel; Director of Franchise Technology Compliance

trigger: A cybersecurity incident is discovered
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee (internal decision, recorded with date and reasoning)

trigger: The company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing to investors), describing the material aspects of nature, scope, timing, and material or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company

trigger: Information required by Item 1.05(a) was not determined or not available when the 8-K was filed
deadline: Within 4 business days after the information is determined (without unreasonable delay) or becomes available
notify: SEC (amended 8-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the original filing said information was not yet determined
clock_starts: Date the information is determined or available

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines in writing that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC
deadline: Delay up to 30 days, extendable by up to 30 more days, and in extraordinary circumstances up to 60 more days, each on a written Attorney General determination
notify: Request through outside counsel to the Department of Justice
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K
notify: SEC (risk management, strategy, and governance disclosure)

trigger: Workforce learn of a potential material cybersecurity incident
deadline: Immediately on knowledge
notify: Disclosure committee members, responders, and executives with knowledge

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering an extortion or ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if extortion occurs. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Suspected card compromise
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: U.S. Secret Service (as named in the Visa document); FBI field office or IC3

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed size criterion would cover the company if the rule is finalized as proposed
clock_starts: Not applicable until a final rule takes effect

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors, except a Visa-required PFI)
notify: Carrier breach hotline

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article, in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
